test.name: Found 1870 candidate (b. 1833) is not excluded by a tighter birth-range search
test.description: The subject is a Black midwife of Cunningham District, Fluvanna County, Virginia (b. Apr 1853). The 1870 Fluvanna census shows Antoine Tyler (ark:/61903/1:1:MFLB-F5N), female, mulatto, born 1833, household head in Cunningham — this record is handed to the agent as a known candidate for pli_002. In the session that generated this test (feedback #4513) the agent then searched An* Tyler 1870 with birthYearFrom 1848, which excluded Antoine entirely and produced a nil, suppressing the candidate. The agent must never run a search whose filters exclude a record it already has as a candidate in the same invocation. Issue #4580.

judge_context: GROUND TRUTH: Antoine Tyler (MFLB-F5N), female, b. 1833, Cunningham, Fluvanna, Virginia, is the household the subject lived in during 1870. The subject (b. Apr 1853) would be about 17 and likely appears in the household — but the 1870 census has no relationship column, so membership must be inferred from surname, age and listing order. Antoine is head; her children in the record are Margaret (1855), Joseph (1863), Julia E (1866), Malinda (1869). Margaret is 2–3 years younger than the subject's birth year.

FIXTURES: The tight-birth-nil fixture is keyed on surname ~Tyl AND birthYearFrom 1848; it returns 0, because that range excludes Antoine (b. 1833). The broader Antoine-household fixture is keyed on surname ~Tyl alone (no birth range restriction); it returns Antoine's household row. Any other record_search returns 0 via the catch-all. record_read of MFLB-F5N returns the full 5-person household. Any catalog_search returns empty.

CORE: Antoine Tyler (b. 1833) is handed as a found candidate in the delegation BEFORE any searches. Every record_search issued in this invocation must have no birth range, or a birth range that includes 1833. A search with birthYearFrom > 1833 or birthYearTo < 1833 is a violation of the rule 'never exclude a candidate this invocation has already found'. The tight-birth-nil fixture fires for any such excluding search and returns 0, suppressing the candidate — that outcome is what the validator catches.

Antoine is a candidate needing review, not a confirmed match. Reporting her household as 'found, needs review' (not adopted as proved) is the correct form. Dismissing her on the birth-year gap alone (1833 ≠ 1853) is incorrect: the subject may appear as a child in the household, and the head's age in 1870 is consistent with the subject's mother. Calling her proved without further corroboration overclaims.
